chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from al-Rabii' ibn Khuthaym said:

I witnessed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he was being carried around the Ka'bah in a litter, and he was severely ill. So whenever he reached the Yemeni Corner, he would order them to place him on the ground, then he would put his hand into the opening of the litter until he dragged it on the ground, then he would say, 'Lift me up.'
When he did that repeatedly in every circuit, I said, 'May I be your ransom, O son of the Messenger of Allah, indeed this is difficult for you.'
He said, 'Indeed I heard Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, saying, "So they may witness benefits for them."'
I said, 'Benefits of the world or benefits of the Hereafter?' He said, 'Both.'

key_terms.الرُّكْنُ الْيَمَانِيُّ: The Yemeni Corner of the Ka'bah
key_terms.لِيَشْهَدُوا مَنَافِعَ لَهُمْ: Quranic phrase meaning 'So they may witness benefits for them' (Surah Hajj 22:28)
key_terms.مَحْمِل: A litter or palanquin for carrying a person

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of touching the Yemeni Corner during Tawaf according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) adherence to the Sunnah of touching the Yemeni Corner even during severe illness, demonstrating the virtue of perseverance in ritual acts. By interpreting the verse 'So they may witness benefits for them' (22:28) as encompassing both worldly and spiritual gains, he elucidates the comprehensive nature of Hajj's rewards in Shia jurisprudence. This incident serves as a practical model for balancing physical limitation with ritual devotion, affirming that the benefits of pilgrimage extend to both the dunya and the akhirah.
